sync.description: Upload the catalog export to update products in bulk. Nothing is written until you review the changes and apply them.
sync.fileHint: Columns: sourceId (required), name, categorySourceId, categoryName, price, stock, taxRate. Prices are whole numbers in cents; stock is a whole number of pieces and may be negative; taxRate is a percent such as 7 or 5,5, and an empty cell means the standard rate. A customer tier's price list is its own column, written “price:” plus the tier's sync key — see Customer tiers.
sync.changeFile: Drop another file, or click to change
sync.previewError: That file could not be read.

formatErrors.no-file: No file was sent. Please choose a file and try again.
formatErrors.file-too-large: That file is too large to upload. Split the export into smaller files.
formatErrors.no-header-row: That file has no header row, so its columns cannot be read.
formatErrors.malformed-quotes: A quotation mark is opened and never closed around line {row}, so the rest of the file cannot be read. Check that every “ has its closing mark, and that a quotation mark inside a value is doubled.
formatErrors.duplicate-column: The column “{column}” appears more than once, so it is unclear which one counts.
formatErrors.unknown-columns: These columns are not recognised: {columns}. Expected any of: {expected}.
formatErrors.too-many-rows: That file has {rows} rows; the limit is {limit}. Split it into smaller files.

rowErrors.cannot-create-product: This product is new, and a new product needs a name, a price and a category.

customers.uploadDescription: Import customer details from a file — their price list, their company details, and whether they may sign in. Nothing is written, and nobody is emailed, until you review the changes and apply them. New accounts are created without a password: each person is sent a link to set their own.
customers.fileHint: Columns: {columns}. sourceId is required and is the key the customer is matched by. access is “enabled” or “disabled”; sendPasswordLink is “yes” or “no”. An empty cell leaves the field as it is — it never clears it.

mode.fullHint: The file carries whole customer records. Price lists and company details are updated, and customers the shop doesn’t have yet are invited — each of them by email.
mode.tiersHint: The file only says which price list each customer is charged. Nobody is invited, nobody is emailed, and nobody’s access changes.

option.createMissing: Invite customers who don’t have an account yet
option.updateExisting: Update customers who already have an account
option.claimByEmail: Claim accounts by email address — where the key is unknown but somebody registered here with that address, adopt their account instead of skipping the row

rowErrors.missing-source-id: This row has no sourceId, so there is no account to match it to.
rowErrors.duplicate-source-id: This sourceId appears earlier in the run; only the first row for it is used.
rowErrors.duplicate-email: Two rows in this run claim the address {email}; only the first is used.
rowErrors.email-taken: Another account already uses {email}. Accounts are matched by their sourceId, so this row would need a different address.
rowErrors.account-unclaimed: Somebody registered here with {email} and carries no source key yet — almost certainly this customer. Turn on “claim accounts by email address” to adopt that account, or give it its key in the account editor.
rowErrors.account-unknown: This row names account {accountId}, and no account here has that ID. The source system is pointing at something that is not here — nothing else in the row is used to guess what it meant.
rowErrors.account-already-keyed: Account {accountId} already carries a source key of its own, so it is already somebody in the source system. One account cannot answer to two keys.
rowErrors.account-unclaimed-by-id: This row names account {accountId} ({email}), which carries no source key yet. Turn on “claim accounts by ID” to adopt it, or give it its key in the account editor.
rowErrors.unknown-tier: There is no price list “{key}” — this shop has {known}.
rowErrors.cannot-create-account: This customer has no account here yet, and a new one needs an email address to send the set-a-password link to.
rowErrors.account-withdrawn: This customer deleted their account. It is not created again from here — they would have to register themselves.
rowErrors.staff-account: This row points at a staff account. Staff are never customers, and their accounts stay the shop’s to manage.
rowErrors.cannot-send-link: A set-a-password link was asked for, but this account cannot sign in — switch it on in the same run, or first.
rowErrors.company-details-incomplete: A company needs both a name and a company ID; this row has one without the other.
rowErrors.invalid-value: The “{column}” column of this row says “{value}”, which is not something that column can hold. The row is skipped; the rest of the file is not.

customers.claimWarning: Accounts registered on the shop that this run will claim, matched on their email address: {count}. From then on the source key names that person, and the next run can change their price list or switch them off. Check the rows below first.
customers.claimByIdWarning: Accounts this run will claim by the ID the source system named: {count}. That ID came from this shop, so it is a deliberate choice rather than a guess — but it is only as right as the mapping on the other side. From then on the source key names that person.
customers.disableWarning: Customers who will lose access: {count}. They stay in the account list and can be switched back on.

rowErrors.duplicate-reference: Order {reference} appears earlier in this update; only the first instruction for it is used.
rowErrors.order-changed: Order {reference} has moved on since your system read it — it now stands at version {current}. Read it again and send the answer against that version.
rowErrors.order-called-off: The customer called order {reference} off, which they may do at any time before it is answered. It moves on only if your system says it takes the cancellation back.
rowErrors.restore-not-announced: Taking back the customer's cancellation of order {reference} has to write to them and update their order page.
rowErrors.personal-data-removed: Order {reference} has had its personal details removed, so it can no longer be moved or changed.
rowErrors.transition-not-allowed: Order {reference} cannot go there from where it stands.
rowErrors.reason-required: Declining an order has to say why, so the customer can be told.
rowErrors.unknown-product: No product here carries the key {productSourceId}, so it cannot be put on order {reference}.
rowErrors.duplicate-product: The product {productSourceId} is on order {reference} twice.
rowErrors.payment-not-recordable: Nothing is owed on order {reference}, so no payment can be recorded against it.

mode.fullHint: The file lists every product. Names, prices and categories are updated, new products are added, and products missing from the file can be hidden.

page.title: Machine tokens
page.intro: A machine token lets an automated client — a scheduled import, an integration — reach the API without signing in. It is not an account: it has no password, no mailbox and no role, only the things it is allowed to do.

page.intro: A definition makes one product attribute filterable in the shop. Its name has to match the attribute's name on the products exactly — nothing is re-entered, and a definition added today applies to products entered long ago. The counts cover live and unpublished products; deleted ones are left out.

page.title: Attributes in use
page.intro: Every attribute key and value the products carry, whether or not the shop filters by it. Attribute text is matched exactly, so a misspelling sits next to the correct spelling here — rename it and every product carrying it follows. Counts cover live and unpublished products; a rename also rewrites deleted ones.

actions.showCustomerHint: Leave this on unless the step was a mistake you are about to take back — their page should say where the order really is.
actions.markPaid: Also record the payment as received
actions.markPaidHint: For money handed over with the goods. You can take this back afterwards.

confirm.heading: {action}?
confirm.message: This records where the order now stands.
confirm.warning: A payment is recorded against this order. Ending it here does not refund anything — arrange that with the customer directly.

actions.notifyAttachment: The payment instructions on this order are sent with it.
actions.notifyNoDocument: This order is paid by transfer and has no payment instructions on it yet — upload them first if the customer should get them with this message.
actions.error: That did not work. The order may already have been answered — reload the page.

tellCustomer.heading: Customer
tellCustomer.behind: They are looking at {seen}; this order is on {current}.
tellCustomer.emailedNever: No email has gone out about this order.

updateConfirm.heading: Show them where the order is?
updateConfirm.message: Their page moves to the version this order is on. Anything the shop changed since they last looked is on it.

tellCustomer.updateNotify: Email them about it as well

emailConfirm.heading: Email the customer?
emailConfirm.message: They are sent the order exactly as their own page shows it. Nothing about the order changes.

tellCustomer.error: That did not work. Reload the page to see where the order stands.

recordConfirm.heading: Record this order as paid?
recordConfirm.message: Only do this once the money has actually arrived.

clearConfirm.heading: Clear the recorded payment?
clearConfirm.message: Use this only where the payment was recorded by mistake. A refund belongs in your own books.

paymentState.error: That did not work. The payment may already have been recorded — reload the page.

personalData.heading: Personal details
personalData.kept: On the order until its retention period ends.

confirm.heading: Remove the personal details from this order?
confirm.message: The guest's name, contact details, addresses and notes are removed from every version of order {reference}, together with any documents uploaded for it. The order, its lines and its total stay.
confirm.warning: This cannot be undone. The guest's other orders keep their details; find them by email address in the order list.

personalData.error: That did not work. The order may have been reopened — reload the page.

documents.heading: Documents
documents.outdated: Uploaded against version {number}; this order is on {current}.
documents.notifyHint: Sent as a message of its own. Payment instructions travel with it; a summary is linked.
documents.notifyBehind: The customer has not been shown the version this belongs to yet.

notifyConfirm.heading: Email this document to the customer?
notifyConfirm.message: They are sent a short message about it. Nothing about the order changes, and you can send it again later.

documents.paymentHint: Only you can supply these — the shop's own payment details for this order.
documents.summaryHint: The shop system draws one from the order. Upload a file to use that instead.

removeConfirm.heading: Remove this document?
removeConfirm.message: The customer stops seeing the uploaded file. The order summary goes back to the one the shop system draws.

documents.error: That did not work. The file may be too large or of an unsupported type.

page.title: Adjust {reference}
page.intro: Record what you agreed with the customer. This writes a new version of the order; the reference, their link and where the order stands all stay as they are.

adjust.warnPaid: This order is already recorded as paid. Changing what it costs does not move any money — put that right in your own books.
adjust.warnReady: This order is already packed. Changing it now records what the shop did — it does not put the goods back on the shelf.
adjust.warnEnded: This order is over. Changing it records what the shop did — it does not put the order back in the queue, and nothing tells the customer unless you ask it to.
adjust.notify: Write to the customer about this change
adjust.notifyHint: Leave this off if the next step will tell them anyway — confirming the order sends them the changes with it.

lines.empty: An order needs at least one line.

adjust.noteHint: The customer is emailed this, so write it for them.
adjust.noteRequired: Say what changed — the customer is told this.

changes.heading: About to change
changes.pricingPending: The lines and the total cannot be worked out until the form is right.

priceNotice.moved: Line prices that differ from the version on file: {count}. Save this only if that is what was agreed.
priceNotice.offList: Lines priced away from {tier}: {count}. That is allowed — check it is deliberate.

confirm.heading: Save this change?
confirm.message: A new version of the order is recorded. Where the order stands does not change, and the customer is written to only if you asked for it above.

errors.order-changed: Somebody else adjusted this order while you were working on it. Reload the page and start again.
errors.no-change: Nothing here differs from the order as it stands. A note on its own is not a change — put what you agreed into the lines or the details first.
errors.unknown-product: One of the lines names a product that no longer exists.
errors.unknown-tier: That price list no longer exists.
errors.invalid-company-id: That registration number is not in a format this shop accepts.
errors.unsupported-country: This shop does not deliver to that country.
errors.invalid-postal-code: That postcode is not the right shape for its country.
errors.unknown-pickup-location: That collection point no longer exists.
errors.billing-details-required: A bank transfer is invoiced to a company, which needs its registration number.
errors.cash-not-available: A company is invoiced by bank transfer, never paid in cash or by card.
errors.billing-address-required: This shop invoices an address of its own, so the order needs one.
errors.order-not-found: There is no order with that reference.
errors.unknown: That did not work. Please try again.

list.loadError: The account list could not be loaded. Please try again.
list.filterCompanyIdFormat: Filter by kind of registration number
list.saveError: That change could not be saved. Please try again.

errors.account-not-found: This account no longer exists. Reload the page to see the current list.
errors.account-not-pending: This registration has already been decided on.
errors.account-closed: This account is closed and can no longer be edited.
errors.email-taken: That email address already has an account.
errors.account-not-approved: Only an approved account can be deactivated. Approve or decline this registration instead.
errors.account-not-disabled: This account is not deactivated, so there is nothing to switch back on.
errors.account-cannot-sign-in: This account cannot sign in, so there is nothing to send. Switch it back on first, or decide on the registration.
errors.self-deactivate: You cannot deactivate your own account.
errors.self-demote: You cannot take the admin role from your own account.
errors.last-admin: This is the only admin account. Another admin must exist before this one can be changed.
errors.account-not-purgeable: Only a registration nobody has decided on can be declined. Deactivate this account instead.
errors.self-delete: You cannot delete your own account here. Delete it from your account page instead.
errors.account-pending: This registration has not been decided on yet. Decline it instead, which removes it entirely.
errors.source-id-taken: Another account already carries that source key. Each key names exactly one account.
errors.role-change-admin-only: Only an admin can change the role of an account.
errors.staff-create-admin-only: Only an admin can create a staff account.
errors.source-id-change-admin-only: Only an admin can change the source key of an account.
errors.not-exemptable: This deployment lets no account of this role skip the sign-in code.

deactivateConfirm.heading: Deactivate account
deactivateConfirm.message: Deactivate {name}? They are signed out immediately and cannot sign in again, and any password link they were sent is cancelled. Their password itself is kept, so switching the account back on returns it as it was. Nothing is deleted, and they are not emailed.

reactivateConfirm.heading: Reactivate account
reactivateConfirm.message: Switch {name} back on? Their details, price tier and password are unchanged, so they can sign in as before — and they are not emailed. An account that never chose a password comes back awaiting one; send them a link from the account page.

declineConfirm.heading: Decline registration
declineConfirm.message: Decline {name}? Their registration and details are removed for good.

editor.emailFixed: The email address is the sign-in name and cannot be changed here.
editor.sourceIdHint: The key the connected system knows this customer by. While it is empty no automated update can reach this account at all.
editor.inviteHint: An email with a link to choose a password is sent when the account is created.
editor.notFound: This account could not be found.
editor.closed: This account is closed. Its details are kept as a record and can no longer be edited.
editor.saveError: This account could not be saved. Please try again.
editor.discardConfirm: Discard the changes to this account?

detail.sourceIdEmpty: None — no automated update can reach this account.
detail.consentsEmpty: No consent recorded for this account.
detail.deleteConsentWithdrawnHint: Recorded as the reason. Leave it clear when they simply asked for the deletion.
detail.deleteError: The account could not be deleted. Please try again.
detail.signInPhoneUnconfirmed: Not confirmed yet. It is confirmed at the next sign-in.
detail.signInPhoneMissing: None that a code can reach. They cannot sign in until staff enter one in the account's details.
detail.signInCodeAlwaysRemembered: At every sign-in, except on a browser they chose to remember (for up to {days} days)
detail.exemptError: The change could not be saved. Please try again.
detail.notFound: This account could not be found.
detail.loadError: This account could not be loaded. Please try again.

deleteConfirm.heading: Delete account on request
deleteConfirm.message: Delete {name} on their request? Their personal details and saved addresses are removed, their past orders are kept with their details removed from them, and they can no longer sign in. They are sent the same confirmation as when they delete it themselves. This cannot be undone.
deleteConfirm.warning: Orders still open stay yours to finish, without the customer's name, phone or address.

exemptConfirm.heading: Exempt from the sign-in code
exemptConfirm.message: Let {name} sign in with the password alone? The exemption is recorded with your name and shown on this page.

unexemptConfirm.heading: Ask for the sign-in code again
unexemptConfirm.message: Ask {name} for the code again from their next sign-in?

page.title: Consents
page.intro: Find the consents a person gave, to answer their own request or an inspection. A search by email address also finds the records of the account that uses it now.

consents.loadError: The records could not be loaded. Please try again.

withdrawErrors.consent-ends-with-account: An account consent is withdrawn by deleting the account.

consents.withdrawError: The withdrawal could not be saved. Please try again.

withdrawConfirm.heading: Enter a withdrawal
withdrawConfirm.message: The consent given by {holder} on {date} ends now and cannot be given back. Its record is kept for the retention period.
withdrawConfirm.warning: The inquiry itself is a mail in the shop's inbox, which this does not touch. Delete it there as well.

maintenance.description: While on, the public shop is hidden from visitors and search engines. You stay signed in and can browse it to preview.
maintenance.statusOn: The shop is hidden from visitors.
maintenance.statusOff: The shop is live and visible to everyone.
maintenance.error: Something went wrong changing maintenance mode. Please try again.

ownership.intro: Hand an area of the shop's data to an external system, or take it back. While an external system owns an area, it is the only thing that writes it: the shop's own way in is turned off, and what it fills is read-only here. While nobody owns it, the shop is in charge and automated updates are refused.

catalog.name: Catalog
catalog.description: Product names, categories, prices and stock. Descriptions, photos, attributes, documents, what is paired with what, and which products the shop shows stay yours either way.
catalog.ownedEffect: File uploads are off, and the fields above are read-only in the catalog editor.
catalog.ownEffect: File uploads work, and automated updates are refused.
catalog.handConfirm: Hand the catalog to an external system?
catalog.handWarning: File uploads stop working, and names, categories, prices and stock become read-only in the catalog editor. Any file already uploaded and waiting can no longer be applied.
catalog.takeConfirm: Take the catalog back from the external system?
catalog.takeWarning: The external system's updates will be refused from its next attempt, and whatever it sends while it is refused is not kept. Hand the catalog back when you are done.

customers.name: Customer accounts
customers.description: Who may sign in, what they are called, the company they buy for and which price list they are on. Their orders are an area of their own.
customers.ownedEffect: Accounts are approved, edited, switched off and switched back on in that system. The lists here still show everything.
customers.ownEffect: Accounts are approved and edited here, and automated updates are refused.
customers.handConfirm: Hand customer accounts to an external system?
customers.handWarning: Approving a registration, editing an account, changing a price list, switching an account off or back on and sending a password link all stop working here and are done in that system instead. Registrations still arrive and are still counted, so you can see who is waiting — but the decision is made over there. Nobody is signed out, and nothing is deleted.
customers.takeConfirm: Take customer accounts back from the external system?
customers.takeWarning: The external system's updates will be refused from its next attempt, and whatever it sends while it is refused is not kept. Anything it had not yet sent — an approval, a price list — you will have to set here yourself.

orders.name: Order processing
orders.description: Answering orders, changing what they say, recording payments and the documents staff put on them. Placing an order and calling off an unanswered one are the customer's own and stay open either way.
orders.ownedEffect: Orders are answered, changed and paid off in that system. The lists and the orders themselves still show everything.
orders.ownEffect: Orders are answered here, and automated updates are refused.
orders.handConfirm: Hand order processing to an external system?
orders.handWarning: Accepting, refusing and moving an order, changing what it says, recording a payment, telling the customer and putting a document on an order all stop working here and are done in that system instead. Orders still arrive and are still counted, and a customer can still call off an order nobody has answered.
orders.takeConfirm: Take order processing back from the external system?
orders.takeWarning: The external system's updates will be refused from its next attempt, and whatever it sends while it is refused is not kept. Anything it had not yet sent — a status, a correction, a payment — you will have to record here yourself.

all.heading: The whole shop
all.description: Every area at once. Areas can also be handed over one at a time below.
all.statusMixed: Partly managed by an external system
all.statusMixedEffect: Areas managed by an external system: {count} of {total}.
all.handConfirm: Hand every area to an external system?
all.handWarning: This does to every area what handing it over one at a time would: the shop's own way into each of them is turned off, and that system becomes the only thing that writes them. Areas it already owns are left as they are.
all.takeConfirm: Take every area back from the external system?
all.takeWarning: The external system's updates will be refused across every area from its next attempt, and whatever it sends while it is refused is not kept. Hand the areas back when you are done.

ownership.error: Something went wrong changing this. Please try again.
ownership.fieldLocked: The catalog is managed by an external system, so this is set there rather than here. To edit it in the shop, take the catalog back under Data ownership in the admin panel.
ownership.fieldLockedShort: Set by the external system that manages the catalog.
ownership.categoryHasProducts: This category still has products in it. While the catalog is managed by an external system, products cannot be moved between categories here — empty it in that system first, or take the catalog back under Data ownership in the admin panel.
ownership.categoryHasDeletedProducts: Deleted products this category still holds: {count}. While the catalog is managed by an external system, they cannot be moved between categories here. A product deleted permanently no longer holds it; one that was ever ordered always will. You can still rename it, change its address and move it to the end of the list.
ownership.productPurge: The external system still sends this product, so deleting it permanently would only bring it back as a new one. It stays deleted.
ownership.productRestore: The external system removed this product because it no longer sends it. It comes back by itself when that system sends it again. To restore it here, take the catalog back under Data ownership in the admin panel.
ownership.productCreate: The catalog is managed by an external system, so new products are added there. To add one in the shop, take the catalog back under Data ownership in the admin panel.
ownership.tierKeyLocked: The catalog is managed by an external system, so this price list's key is set there. The name is yours to change either way, and you can still add a price list or remove an unused one.
ownership.accountLocked: Customer accounts are managed by an external system, so this account is edited there rather than here. To edit it in the shop, take customer accounts back under Data ownership in the admin panel.
ownership.accountCreate: Customer accounts are managed by an external system, so new customers are added there. To add one in the shop, take customer accounts back under Data ownership in the admin panel.
ownership.runStranded: This file was uploaded before the area was handed to an external system, so it can no longer be applied. Discard it, or take the area back under Data ownership in the admin panel.
ownership.accountDecline: Customer accounts are managed by an external system, so registrations are decided there. Decline this one in that system, or take customer accounts back under Data ownership in the admin panel.
ownership.accountActive: Customer accounts are managed by an external system, so switching one off or back on is done there. Change it in that system, or take customer accounts back under Data ownership in the admin panel.
ownership.orderLocked: Orders are managed by an external system, so this one is answered there rather than here. Customers can still place orders and call off ones nobody has answered. To work orders in the shop, take order processing back under Data ownership in the admin panel.
